_comment: Role-class -> permitted model-tier policy for #422's model-vs-role-class audit. Each class's permitted models are a CONTIGUOUS range on fleet-core's ordered MODELS ladder (rank 0 = fable strongest .. rank 3 = haiku weakest, see plugins/fleet-core/scripts/fleet_commons/models.json) between max_model (strongest permitted) and min_model (weakest permitted) -- never an arbitrary unordered set ({#tier-vocab-ordering}). role_tier_aliases maps the existing team-execution `role-tier:` frontmatter vocabulary onto a class; a class's own key (e.g. 'review') is always also a valid role-tier value, so a fixture (or a future real agent) can select a class directly. is_review_class gates tools/agent_spec.py's tool-scope-floor rule (Edit/Write forbidden, tools: required).

review.rationale: Adversarial review/verify judgment agents (team-execution's api-reviewer, architecture-reviewer, security-reviewer, etc.) need opus-grade reasoning; a weaker pin silently degrades review quality. Least-privilege tool floor applies: tools: must be present and exclude Edit/Write.

tester.rationale: Contract/behavior testers (team-execution's api-contract-tester, event-flow-tester, etc.) need at least sonnet; escalation to opus is permitted, never required.

scanner.rationale: Mechanical scanners and monitors (team-execution's api-compat-scanner, dependency-scanner, deploy-watcher, etc.) are cheap deterministic work; pinning opus here is wasteful, not a quality risk.

survey.rationale: Read-only survey/search/sampling agents never need opus-grade judgment. No fleet member carries role-tier: survey today -- reserved for future agents and this lint's red-fixture coverage (a survey agent accidentally pinned to opus must fail the audit).
